# Script introduction

This is the fourth of six R Markdown notebooks. It fits the range-size models of the paper: the main taxonomic mixed models, their geographic adjustments (regional range-size background and spherical GAM), phylogenetic models on matched and genus-grafted trees, joint phylogenetic-spatial models, and the lineage checks (leave-one-genus-out and genus-level PGLS).

The inputs are the species tables and Daru range cells of `s03_build_species_tables`, the occurrence records and range metrics of `s02_prepare_ranges`, the duplicate-species clusters of `s01_prepare_traits`, the GBIF Backbone snapshot and the published trees. The outputs (fitted main models, coefficient, contrast and metadata tables, tree crosswalks, grafted trees, presence cells and species centres) are used by `s05_check_robustness`, `s06_summarise_results` and the report. Model tables keep a `table` column: `MAIN_subtype` is the main species table and `MAIN_daru_subtype` the modelled-range table. A full run takes about 2.5 h, mostly the phylogenetic spatial models and the leave-one-genus-out refits.

# Setup

## Packages

`lmerTest` fits the mixed models and `mgcv` the GAMs; `ape`, `nlme`, `phytools` and `emmeans` are called with `::` (mostly in `code/R`).

```{r load_packages, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(resrepo)
library(data.table)
library(lmerTest)
library(mgcv)
```

## Variables

The three range measures, the main table's label in the model tables, the two trees, and the model formulas and branch lengths of the phylogenetic models are shared by the sections below. The Yumnam tree keeps its published branch lengths, and the Schär tree gets Grafen lengths after pruning.

```{r setup_variables}
# Range measures: short name -> column of the species table
measures <- c(area = "range_area",
              lat = "latitudinal_extent",
              lon = "longitudinal_extent")

# Label of the main species table in the model tables
main_table <- "MAIN_subtype"

# The two trees and the branch lengths each one gets in the phylogenetic models
studies <- c("yumnam_2025", "schar_2018")
branch <- c(yumnam_2025 = "published", schar_2018 = "grafen")

# Formulas of the phylogenetic models: type only, and type plus centred partner breadth
formulas <- list(type = log10_range ~ interaction_type,
                 breadth = log10_range ~ interaction_type + partner_breadth_centered)
```

## Folders

Raw inputs are read from the versioned raw data and earlier results from the folders of `s01_prepare_traits` to `s03_build_species_tables`; outputs are written to this notebook's folder in the versioned intermediate data. The input and output lists of the sections below give paths relative to these folders (`s01/` to `s03/` for the earlier notebooks).

```{r setup_folders}
# Raw data and the outputs of s01 to s03
dir_data_raw <- path_resrepo("data/raw")
dir_s01 <- path_resrepo("data/intermediate/s01_prepare_traits")
dir_s02 <- path_resrepo("data/intermediate/s02_prepare_ranges")
dir_s03 <- path_resrepo("data/intermediate/s03_build_species_tables")

# Outputs of this notebook
dir_data_intermediate <- path_resrepo("data/intermediate/s04_fit_models")
dir.create(dir_data_intermediate, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# The two published trees: Yumnam & Kodandaramaiah (2025) and Schär et al. (2018)
tree_files <- c(
  yumnam_2025 = file.path(
    dir_data_raw, "phylogenies", "yumnam_2025",
    "21Jan2025_30June23_SubfamAdded_RelTime_DivergenceTime_928sp.nwk"),
  schar_2018 = file.path(dir_data_raw, "phylogenies", "schar_2018", "treemacro.nex"))
```

## Functions

`write_table()` writes the output tables. `models.R` fits the taxonomic mixed models and their contrasts, `geography.R` the presence cells, regional background and spherical GAMs, `projections.R` the Equal Earth grids, `name_matching.R` the GBIF Backbone snapshot and `phylogeny.R` the matching of tree tips and the PGLS.

```{r load_functions}
# Output tables
source(here::here("code", "R", "write_table.R"))

# Taxonomic mixed models and their contrasts
source(here::here("code", "R", "models.R"))

# Presence cells, regional background and spherical GAMs
source(here::here("code", "R", "geography.R"))

# Equal Earth grids
source(here::here("code", "R", "projections.R"))

# Published trees, their tip names and PGLS
source(here::here("code", "R", "phylogeny.R"))

# Strict name matching to the GBIF Backbone snapshot
source(here::here("code", "R", "name_matching.R"))
```

The main species table is read with the pool keys as text and the interaction types as factors with the levels n, f, m and p.

```{r define_reader}
# Read the main species table, keeping the pool keys as text and the interaction types as
# a factor with the levels n, f, m and p; returns a data frame
read_species_table <- function() {
  d <- read.csv(file.path(dir_s03, "species_table.csv"),
                na.strings = c("", "NA"),
                colClasses = c(pool_key = "character"))
  d$interaction_type <- factor(d$interaction_type, levels = c("n", "f", "m", "p"))
  d
}
```

Each section below reads its inputs from disk and ends by removing its objects (in a hidden chunk), so only the objects defined in this setup carry over from one section to the next.

```{r keep_setup_objects}
# Objects of the setup, kept when each section clears its own objects
setup_objects <- c(ls(), "setup_objects")
```

# Taxonomic mixed models

Log10 range area, latitudinal extent and longitudinal extent are modelled with interaction type, and with type plus recorded partner breadth (raw count, centred), and nested subfamily/genus random intercepts (lme4, lmerTest). Pairwise type contrasts are Tukey-adjusted (emmeans). The main table is fitted on all ranges and on the 80, 90 and 95 % range-stability subsets; the modelled-range table on all ranges.

*Inputs:* s03/species_table.csv, s03/species_table_daru.csv  
*Outputs:* lmm_coefficients.csv, lmm_contrasts.csv, lmm_metadata.csv (rows tagged by `table`: MAIN_subtype = main table, MAIN_daru_subtype = modelled ranges; and by `analysis`)

```{r fit_taxonomic_models}
# --- Tables and analyses ---
# The main table and the modelled-range table. Analyses use all ranges (main) or the
# 80, 90 and 95 % range-stability subsets (the threshold NULL keeps all ranges)
tables <- c(MAIN_subtype = "species_table.csv",
            MAIN_daru_subtype = "species_table_daru.csv")
analyses <- list(main = NULL,
                 stability_80 = 0.80,
                 stability_90 = 0.90,
                 stability_95 = 0.95)

# Coefficient, contrast and metadata tables of all fits
res <- list(coefficients = list(), contrasts = list(), metadata = list())

# --- Fit the models of every table and analysis ---
for (k in names(tables)) {
  d <- read.csv(file.path(dir_s03, tables[[k]]), na.strings = c("", "NA"))
  d$interaction_type <- factor(d$interaction_type, levels = c("n", "f", "m", "p"))

  for (a in names(analyses)) {
    # Modelled ranges have no stability values, so they get the main models only
    if (!is.null(analyses[[a]]) && !any(is.finite(d$asympt_prop_area))) next

    fit <- fit_log_range_models(d, measures = measures,
                                stability_threshold = analyses[[a]],
                                breadth_scale = "raw")

    # Tag the result tables with the table and the analysis
    for (comp in names(res)) {
      x <- fit[[comp]]
      x$table <- k
      x$analysis <- a
      res[[comp]][[paste(k, a)]] <- x
    }
    cat(k, a, "done\n")
  }
}

# --- Write the result tables ---
for (comp in names(res))
  write_table(rbindlist(res[[comp]], fill = TRUE),
              file.path(dir_data_intermediate, paste0("lmm_", comp, ".csv")))
```

```{r clear_fit_taxonomic_models, include=FALSE}
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), setup_objects))
invisible(gc())
```

# Main models for the report

The main models are refitted and saved with their coefficient, estimated-mean, contrast and metadata tables for the report tables and figures; the section checks that the contrasts reproduce those of the taxonomic mixed models.

*Inputs:* s03/species_table.csv; lmm_contrasts.csv  
*Outputs:* main_models.rds (list of six lmerModLmerTest fits named area_type, area_breadth, lat_type, lat_breadth, lon_type, lon_breadth), main_coefficients.csv, main_estimated_means.csv, main_contrasts.csv, main_metadata.csv

```{r save_main_models}
# --- Refit the main models ---
# The saved models carry their input data, which the report and the later notebooks use.
d <- read_species_table()
fit <- fit_log_range_models(d, measures = measures, breadth_scale = "raw")

# --- Save the models and their tables ---
saveRDS(fit$models, file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "main_models.rds"))
for (comp in c("coefficients", "estimated_means", "contrasts", "metadata"))
  write_table(fit[[comp]],
              file.path(dir_data_intermediate, paste0("main_", comp, ".csv")))

# --- Check against the taxonomic mixed models ---
# The contrasts must reproduce those of the main analysis in lmm_contrasts.csv
ref <- fread(file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "lmm_contrasts.csv"))[
  table == main_table & analysis == "main"]
chk <- merge(as.data.table(fit$contrasts)[, .(measure, predictors, contrast,
                                              r1 = range_ratio)],
             ref[, .(measure, predictors, contrast, r2 = range_ratio)],
             by = c("measure", "predictors", "contrast"))
stopifnot(nrow(chk) == nrow(ref), max(abs(chk$r1 / chk$r2 - 1)) < 1e-8)
cat("main models saved; n (area, type model):", nrow(fit$model_data$area_type), "\n")
```

```{r clear_save_main_models, include=FALSE}
invisible(gc())
```

# Geographic models

Range units occupy 200-km and 500-km Equal Earth cells, and each gets an equal-cell-weighted centre. The regional background is the mean log10 modelled range of all co-occurring butterflies (Daru 2025) except the focal genus, in 500-km cells with at least five comparison species; it enters the mixed models as a covariate. The spherical GAM adds an isotropic smooth of the species centre on the sphere (mgcv `sos` basis) to subfamily and genus random effects.

*Inputs:* s02/records_final.rds, s02/range_metrics.csv; s03/species_table.csv, s03/analysis_units.csv, s03/daru_all_species.csv, s03/daru_cells_500km.csv  
*Outputs:* presence_200km.csv, presence_500km.csv, species_centres.csv, background_{coefficients,contrasts,metadata}.csv, gam_{coefficients,contrasts,metadata}.csv (rows tagged table = MAIN_subtype and analysis)

## Presence cells and species centres

Equal Earth cells occupied by the records of the main cleaning are listed at 200 and 500 km. Each range unit's centre is the equal-cell-weighted spherical centre of its 200-km cells: the normalised vector mean of the cells, or their spherical medoid (among at most 500 evenly spaced candidate cells) when the mean vector is shorter than 0.05, as for very widespread or symmetric distributions.

```{r presence_cells_and_centres}
# --- Records of the main cleaning, by range pool ---
# Unique record coordinates of each pool (a list of data frames named by pool key)
x <- readRDS(file.path(dir_s02, "records_final.rds"))
x <- unique(x[in_main == TRUE & !is.na(pool_key),
              .(pool_key, decimalLongitude, decimalLatitude)])
occ <- split(as.data.frame(x[, .(decimalLongitude, decimalLatitude)]), x$pool_key)
rm(x)
invisible(gc())

# --- Occupied cells at 200 and 500 km ---
presence_200 <- equal_area_species_cells(occ, cell_km = 200)
write_table(presence_200, file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "presence_200km.csv"))

# The 500-km cells have their own grid: they do not nest in the 200-km cells
presence_500 <- equal_area_species_cells(occ, cell_km = 500)
write_table(presence_500, file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "presence_500km.csv"))
rm(occ)
invisible(gc())

# --- Range pools with a range area ---
# One row per pool; only these pools get a centre
ranges <- read.csv(file.path(dir_s02, "range_metrics.csv"),
                   colClasses = c(pool_key = "character"))
ranges <- ranges[!duplicated(ranges$pool_key) & is.finite(ranges$range_area), ]
ranges$species <- ranges$pool_key

# --- Species centres ---
# One row per pool: the equal-cell-weighted spherical centre of its 200-km cells, the
# method used, the length of the mean vector (resultant) and the number of occupied cells
centre_cells <- presence_200[presence_200$species %in% ranges$species, ]
centres <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(centre_cells, centre_cells$species), function(d) {
  # Cell centres as unit vectors on the sphere
  lon <- d$cell_longitude * pi / 180
  lat <- d$cell_latitude * pi / 180
  xyz <- cbind(cos(lat) * cos(lon), cos(lat) * sin(lon), sin(lat))

  # Mean vector and its length
  vector <- colMeans(xyz)
  resultant <- sqrt(sum(vector^2))

  if (is.finite(resultant) && resultant >= 0.05) {
    # Normalised mean vector, converted back to longitude and latitude
    centre <- vector / resultant
    centre_lon <- atan2(centre[2], centre[1]) * 180 / pi
    centre_lat <- atan2(centre[3], sqrt(sum(centre[1:2]^2))) * 180 / pi
    method <- "spherical_centroid"
  } else {
    # Spherical medoid when the mean vector is short (very widespread or symmetric
    # distributions): the candidate cell with the smallest summed angular distance to all
    # cells, among at most 500 evenly spaced candidates
    candidate_id <- if (nrow(xyz) <= 500L) seq_len(nrow(xyz)) else
      unique(round(seq(1, nrow(xyz), length.out = 500L)))
    distances <- acos(pmax(-1, pmin(1, xyz[candidate_id, , drop = FALSE] %*% t(xyz))))
    medoid <- candidate_id[which.min(rowSums(distances))]
    centre_lon <- d$cell_longitude[medoid]
    centre_lat <- d$cell_latitude[medoid]
    method <- if (length(candidate_id) == nrow(xyz)) "spherical_medoid" else
      "candidate_spherical_medoid"
  }

  data.frame(species = d$species[1],
             geo_longitude = centre_lon, geo_latitude = centre_lat,
             centre_method = method, centre_resultant = resultant,
             occupied_cells = nrow(d))
}))
write_table(centres, file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "species_centres.csv"))
```

## All-butterfly regional background (500-km cells)

The background of a unit is the mean log10 modelled range of the co-occurring butterflies (Daru 2025) outside its genus, in cells with at least five comparison species, cells weighted equally. Comparators from all butterfly families dilute the trait under test, which a background of the analysed lycaenids would partly contain. The genus left out is the unit's revised genus as an analysis unit, else its GBIF genus.

```{r regional_background}
# --- Genus left out of each background ---
# The revised genus of the analysis unit, else the GBIF genus
units <- read.csv(file.path(dir_s03, "analysis_units.csv"),
                  colClasses = c(pool_key = "character"))
unit_genus <- units$genus[match(ranges$pool_key, units$pool_key)]
genus_of <- setNames(ifelse(is.na(unit_genus), ranges$genus, unit_genus), ranges$species)

# --- Background of each unit ---
# Mean log10 modelled range of the co-occurring butterflies outside the unit's genus, in
# 500-km cells with at least five comparison species
background <- butterfly_range_background(
  presence_500[presence_500$species %in% ranges$species, ], genus_of,
  fread(file.path(dir_s03, "daru_all_species.csv")),
  fread(file.path(dir_s03, "daru_cells_500km.csv")),
  measures = measures, min_other = 5L)
```

## Models

The background enters the mixed models as a covariate; the spherical GAM adds an isotropic smooth of the species centre to subfamily and genus random effects.

```{r fit_geographic_models}
# --- Species table with the regional background and the species centres ---
d <- read_species_table()

# Geographic values only where the unit kept its range
has_range <- is.finite(d$range_area)

# Regional background columns, matched to the units by pool key
key <- match(d$pool_key, background$species)
d_background <- d
for (cc in grep("^regional_background_", names(background), value = TRUE))
  d_background[[cc]] <- ifelse(has_range, background[[cc]][key], NA)

# Species-centre columns: numeric ones follow the same rule, other columns are copied
key <- match(d$pool_key, centres$species)
d_centres <- d
for (cc in setdiff(names(centres), "species"))
  d_centres[[cc]] <- if (is.numeric(centres[[cc]]))
    ifelse(has_range, centres[[cc]][key], NA) else centres[[cc]][key]

# Result tables of all fits
res <- list(background_coefficients = list(),
            background_contrasts = list(),
            background_metadata = list(),
            gam_coefficients = list(),
            gam_contrasts = list(),
            gam_metadata = list())

# --- Mixed models with the regional background ---
rf <- fit_log_range_models(d_background, measures = measures,
                           regional_background = TRUE, breadth_scale = "raw")
for (comp in c("coefficients", "contrasts", "metadata")) {
  x <- rf[[comp]]
  x$table <- main_table
  x$analysis <- "regional_background_500_bfly"
  res[[paste0("background_", comp)]][[1]] <- x
}

# --- Spherical GAMs ---
# Isotropic smooth of the species centre on the sphere plus subfamily and genus random
# effects
for (m in names(measures)) for (pred in c("type", "breadth")) {
  g <- fit_species_spatial_gam(d_centres, measures[[m]],
                               include_breadth = pred == "breadth")
  for (comp in c("coefficients", "contrasts", "metadata")) {
    x <- g[[comp]]
    x$table <- main_table
    x$measure <- m
    x$predictors <- pred
    x$analysis <- "spherical_gam"
    res[[paste0("gam_", comp)]][[paste(m, pred)]] <- x
  }
  cat("spherical GAM", m, pred, "done\n")
}

# --- Write the result tables ---
for (comp in names(res))
  write_table(rbindlist(res[[comp]], fill = TRUE),
              file.path(dir_data_intermediate, paste0(comp, ".csv")))
cat("units with a background (area):",
    sum(is.finite(background$regional_background_area)),
    "; with a centre:", nrow(centres), "\n")
```

```{r clear_fit_geographic_models, include=FALSE}

invisible(gc())
```

# Tree-tip crosswalks

Species of the main table are linked to the tips of the Yumnam & Kodandaramaiah (2025) and Schär et al. (2018) trees, first through the GBIF Backbone snapshot (`match_tree_tips()`: the binomial parsed from a tip is an accepted name or a synonym of one accepted species, whose duplicate cluster the unit represents), then by exact binomial; each tip links to one species at most. No taxon names are queried online.

*Inputs:* s03/species_table.csv; s01/species_traits.csv (duplicate clusters); gbif_backbone/ snapshot; taxonomy/riodinid_genera.csv; phylogenies/ trees  
*Outputs:* crosswalk_yumnam_2025.csv, crosswalk_schar_2018.csv

```{r match_tree_tips}
# --- Trees, species table and GBIF Backbone snapshot ---
trees <- lapply(tree_files, read_published_tree)
d <- read_species_table()
snapshot <- read_backbone_snapshot(dir_data_raw)

# Representative key of each accepted key (duplicate clusters of s01)
traits <- read.csv(file.path(dir_s01, "species_traits.csv"), colClasses = "character",
                   na.strings = c("", "NA"))
representative_of <- setNames(traits$representative_key, traits$gbif_key)

# --- Match the units to the tips of each tree ---
for (study in names(trees)) {
  # Route 1: the tip that the snapshot resolves to the unit (one tip per species)
  tips <- match_tree_tips(trees[[study]], study, snapshot, representative_of)
  tips <- tips[tips$matched, ]
  tip_via_key <- tips$tree_tip_original[match(sprintf("%.0f", d$gbif_key),
                                              tips$representative_key)]

  # Route 2: exact parsed binomial of the unit's name, ignoring binomials shared by
  # several tips
  tip_labels <- trees[[study]]$tip.label
  parsed <- vapply(tip_labels,
                   function(t) standardise_species_label(species_name_from_tip(t)),
                   "")
  parsed[duplicated(parsed) | duplicated(parsed, fromLast = TRUE)] <- NA
  tip_exact <- tip_labels[match(standardise_species_label(d$species), parsed)]

  # Route 1 takes precedence
  tip <- ifelse(is.na(tip_via_key), tip_exact, tip_via_key)
  map <- data.frame(analysis_species = d$species,
                    tree_tip_original = tip,
                    match_route = ifelse(!is.na(tip_via_key), "gbif_key",
                                         ifelse(!is.na(tip_exact), "exact_binomial", NA)))

  # First unit keeps the tip
  map$tree_tip_original[duplicated(map$tree_tip_original) &
                          !is.na(map$tree_tip_original)] <- NA
  map$matched <- !is.na(map$tree_tip_original)
  write_table(map, file.path(dir_data_intermediate, paste0("crosswalk_", study, ".csv")))
  cat(study, ": tips matched to a species ", nrow(tips),
      "; units matched ", sum(map$matched),
      " (via GBIF key ", sum(map$matched & map$match_route %in% "gbif_key"),
      ")\n", sep = "")
}
```

```{r clear_match_tree_tips, include=FALSE}
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), setup_objects))
invisible(gc())
```

# Matched-tip PGLS

Pagel-lambda PGLS (REML, lambda profiled over [0, 1]) and the taxonomic mixed models are fitted to the same matched species on each tree; the Yumnam tree keeps its published branch lengths and the Schär tree gets Grafen lengths after pruning.

*Inputs:* s03/species_table.csv; crosswalk_<tree>.csv; phylogenies/ trees  
*Outputs:* pgls_matched_{coefficients,contrasts,metadata}.csv (PGLS) and pgls_matched_lmm_{contrasts,metadata}.csv (mixed models on the same species); rows tagged table = MAIN_subtype and study

```{r fit_matched_pgls}
# --- Trees and the main species table ---
trees <- lapply(tree_files, read_published_tree)
d_all <- read_species_table()

# PGLS tables, and mixed-model tables for the same species
res <- list(coefficients = list(),
            contrasts = list(),
            metadata = list(),
            lmm_contrasts = list(),
            lmm_metadata = list())

# --- Fit the models on the species matched to each tree ---
for (study in names(branch)) {
  map <- read.csv(file.path(dir_data_intermediate, paste0("crosswalk_", study, ".csv")),
                  na.strings = c("", "NA"))
  matched <- d_all[d_all$species %in% map$analysis_species[map$matched], , drop = FALSE]

  # Taxonomic mixed models on the matched species
  tax <- fit_log_range_models(matched, measures = measures, breadth_scale = "raw")
  for (comp in c("contrasts", "metadata")) {
    x <- tax[[comp]]
    x$table <- main_table
    x$study <- study
    res[[paste0("lmm_", comp)]][[study]] <- x
  }

  # PGLS of each measure and predictor set, on the data of the corresponding mixed model
  for (key in names(tax$model_data)) {
    # The model key is the measure and the predictors
    fields <- strsplit(key, "_", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
    d <- tax$model_data[[key]]
    meta <- tax$metadata[tax$metadata$measure == fields[1] &
                           tax$metadata$predictors == fields[2], ]

    # The reference partner breadth of the breadth models is 1 (centred: 1 minus the mean
    # breadth). A failed fit is reported and skipped.
    fit <- tryCatch(
      fit_pagel_pgls(d, trees[[study]], map, formulas[[fields[2]]], study = study,
                     measure = fields[1], predictors = fields[2],
                     branch_treatment = branch[[study]],
                     breadth_reference_centered = if (fields[2] == "breadth")
                       1 - meta$partner_breadth_mean else 0,
                     breadth_reference_original = if (fields[2] == "breadth") 1 else NA,
                     method = "REML"),
      error = function(e) {
        message(study, " ", key, ": ", conditionMessage(e))
        NULL
      })
    if (is.null(fit)) next

    for (comp in c("coefficients", "contrasts", "metadata")) {
      x <- fit[[comp]]
      x$table <- main_table
      x$study <- study
      res[[comp]][[paste(study, key)]] <- x
    }
  }
  cat(study, "done", format(Sys.time(), "%H:%M:%S"), "\n")
}

# --- Write the result tables ---
for (comp in names(res))
  write_table(rbindlist(res[[comp]], fill = TRUE),
              file.path(dir_data_intermediate, paste0("pgls_matched_", comp, ".csv")))
```

```{r clear_fit_matched_pgls, include=FALSE}

invisible(gc())
```

# Genus-grafted PGLS

Analysed species missing from a tree are grafted onto their genus, which retains most analysed species and parasites; PGLS as above. The grafted trees are saved for the later phylogenetic analyses.

*Inputs:* s03/species_table.csv; crosswalk_<tree>.csv; phylogenies/ trees  
*Outputs:* pgls_grafted_{coefficients,contrasts,metadata,coverage}.csv; grafted_trees.rds (list of the two grafted trees, tips = analysis species, attribute `grafted` = grafted species)

`graft_species_to_genus()` adds the analysed species missing from a tree to their genus; it is applied to both trees.

```{r define_graft_species_to_genus}
#' Graft analysed species that are missing from a tree onto their genus
#'
#' Species are added in alphabetical order. A species whose genus has two or
#' more tips is attached at the most recent common ancestor of its congeners
#' (a polytomy at the genus node, as in `phytools::add.species.to.genus(where =
#' "root")`, but matching genera exactly at the start of the label); a species
#' whose genus has one tip becomes its sister, splitting that tip's branch at
#' its midpoint. The tree is made ultrametric first (`force.ultrametric`,
#' method "extend") if necessary, and new branches keep it ultrametric.
#' Species of genera absent from the tree are not grafted.
#' @param tree Ultrametric `phylo` tree whose tip labels are analysis names
#'   (`Genus_species`).
#' @param species Analysis names that should be on the tree.
#' @param genus_map Optional named character vector (analysis name -> genus) giving the
#'   genus of tips and of species to graft, for names whose current genus differs from the
#'   genus in the name (revised classification). Names not in the map use the genus at the
#'   start of the label.
#' @return The grafted tree; attribute `grafted` lists the added species.
graft_species_to_genus <- function(tree, species, genus_map = NULL) {
  # Make the tree ultrametric if it is not
  if (!ape::is.ultrametric(tree))
    tree <- phytools::force.ultrametric(tree, method = "extend")

  # Genus of tip labels or species names: the genus map where it has an entry, else the
  # genus at the start of the name
  genus_of <- function(x) {
    g <- sub("_.*", "", x)
    if (!is.null(genus_map)) {
      m <- unname(genus_map[x])
      g[!is.na(m)] <- m[!is.na(m)]
    }
    g
  }

  # --- Graft the missing species in alphabetical order ---
  grafted <- character()
  for (s in sort(setdiff(species, tree$tip.label))) {
    # Species of genera absent from the tree are skipped
    ii <- which(genus_of(tree$tip.label) == genus_of(s))
    if (!length(ii)) next

    if (length(ii) > 1L) {
      # Two or more congeners: polytomy at their most recent common ancestor
      node <- phytools::findMRCA(tree, tree$tip.label[ii])
      tree <- phytools::bind.tip(tree, s, where = node)
    } else {
      # One congener: sister to it, splitting its branch at the midpoint
      half <- 0.5 * tree$edge.length[tree$edge[, 2] == ii]
      tree <- phytools::bind.tip(tree, s, where = ii, position = half)
    }
    grafted <- c(grafted, s)
  }

  # The grafted species are recorded as an attribute
  attr(tree, "grafted") <- grafted
  tree
}
```

```{r fit_grafted_pgls}
# --- Trees and analysed species ---
trees <- lapply(tree_files, read_published_tree)
d_all <- read_species_table()

# Units with a type, genus and subfamily and a range area or latitudinal extent
analysed <- d_all$species[!is.na(d_all$interaction_type) & !is.na(d_all$genus) &
                            !is.na(d_all$subfamily) &
                            (is.finite(d_all$range_area) |
                               is.finite(d_all$latitudinal_extent))]

# Result tables and the grafted tree of each study
res <- list(coefficients = list(),
            contrasts = list(),
            metadata = list(),
            coverage = list())
grafted_trees <- list()

# --- Graft each tree and fit the models ---
for (study in names(branch)) {
  map <- read.csv(file.path(dir_data_intermediate, paste0("crosswalk_", study, ".csv")),
                  na.strings = c("", "NA"))
  matched <- intersect(analysed, map$analysis_species[map$matched])

  # A missing species joins its congeners' most recent common ancestor as a polytomy, or
  # becomes sister to a single congener at the midpoint of its branch; species of genera
  # absent from the tree are omitted. Grafen lengths (Schär) are computed on the pruned
  # matched tree before grafting. Tips and grafted species take the revised genus of the
  # analysis table.
  tr <- graft_species_to_genus(
    prepare_analysis_tree(trees[[study]], map, matched, branch[[study]]),
    analysed,
    genus_map = setNames(d_all$genus, d_all$species))
  grafted_trees[[study]] <- tr

  # Crosswalk of the grafted tree (every tip is its own analysis species) and its coverage
  cw <- data.frame(analysis_species = tr$tip.label,
                   tree_tip_original = tr$tip.label,
                   matched = TRUE)
  res$coverage[[study]] <- data.frame(study = study,
                                      analysed = length(analysed),
                                      matched = length(matched),
                                      grafted = length(attr(tr, "grafted")),
                                      on_tree = length(tr$tip.label))

  # Taxonomic mixed models on the species of the grafted tree
  d <- d_all[d_all$species %in% tr$tip.label, ]
  tax <- fit_log_range_models(d, measures = measures, breadth_scale = "raw")

  # PGLS of each measure and predictor set
  for (key in names(tax$model_data)) {
    # The model key is the measure and the predictors
    fields <- strsplit(key, "_", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
    dm <- tax$model_data[[key]]
    meta <- tax$metadata[tax$metadata$measure == fields[1] &
                           tax$metadata$predictors == fields[2], ]

    # The grafted tree already has its final branch lengths, so they are used as given
    # ("published"). A failed fit is reported and skipped.
    fit <- tryCatch(
      fit_pagel_pgls(dm, tr, cw, formulas[[fields[2]]], study = study,
                     measure = fields[1], predictors = fields[2],
                     branch_treatment = "published", method = "REML",
                     breadth_reference_centered = if (fields[2] == "breadth")
                       1 - meta$partner_breadth_mean else 0,
                     breadth_reference_original = if (fields[2] == "breadth") 1 else NA),
      error = function(e) {
        message(study, " ", key, ": ", conditionMessage(e))
        NULL
      })
    if (is.null(fit)) next

    # Tag the result tables; the metadata also records the number of grafted species
    n_graft <- sum(dm$species %in% attr(tr, "grafted"))
    for (comp in c("coefficients", "contrasts", "metadata")) {
      x <- fit[[comp]]
      x$table <- main_table
      x$study <- study
      x$tree_set <- "grafted"

      # Record the branch lengths actually used
      if ("branch_treatment" %in% names(x)) x$branch_treatment <- branch[[study]]
      if (comp == "metadata") x$n_grafted <- n_graft
      res[[comp]][[paste(study, key)]] <- x
    }
    cat(study, key, "n =", nrow(dm), "grafted =", n_graft,
        format(Sys.time(), "%H:%M:%S"), "\n")
  }
}

# --- Write the result tables and the grafted trees ---
for (comp in names(res))
  write_table(rbindlist(res[[comp]], fill = TRUE),
              file.path(dir_data_intermediate, paste0("pgls_grafted_", comp, ".csv")))
saveRDS(grafted_trees, file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "grafted_trees.rds"))
print(rbindlist(res$coverage))
```

```{r clear_fit_grafted_pgls, include=FALSE}
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), setup_objects))
invisible(gc())
```

# Joint phylogenetic and spatial models

On the grafted trees, a GAM combines the spherical smooth with a species random effect with phylogenetic covariance, and a PGLS includes the all-butterfly regional background. Moran's I of the residuals between species centres within 500 km is recorded for these models and the plain grafted PGLS.

*Inputs:* grafted_trees.rds, presence_500km.csv, species_centres.csv; s02/range_metrics.csv; s03/species_table.csv, s03/analysis_units.csv, s03/daru_all_species.csv, s03/daru_cells_500km.csv  
*Outputs:* phylo_geography_contrasts.csv, phylo_geography_moran.csv

```{r fit_phylo_spatial_models}
# --- Grafted trees ---
grafted <- readRDS(file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "grafted_trees.rds"))

# --- All-butterfly background, as in the geographic models ---
ranges <- read.csv(file.path(dir_s02, "range_metrics.csv"),
                   colClasses = c(pool_key = "character"))
ranges <- ranges[!duplicated(ranges$pool_key) & is.finite(ranges$range_area), ]
p5 <- read.csv(file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "presence_500km.csv"),
               colClasses = c(species = "character"))
p5 <- p5[p5$species %in% ranges$pool_key, ]
units <- read.csv(file.path(dir_s03, "analysis_units.csv"),
                  colClasses = c(pool_key = "character"))
unit_genus <- units$genus[match(ranges$pool_key, units$pool_key)]
bg <- butterfly_range_background(
  p5,
  setNames(ifelse(is.na(unit_genus), ranges$genus, unit_genus), ranges$pool_key),
  fread(file.path(dir_s03, "daru_all_species.csv")),
  fread(file.path(dir_s03, "daru_cells_500km.csv")),
  measures = measures)

# --- Species centres and Moran's I ---
ce <- fread(file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "species_centres.csv"),
            colClasses = c(species = "character"))

# Moran's I of residuals `res` with neighbours defined as species centres within 500 km
# (binary weights). `keys` are the pool keys of the residuals, in the same order;
# residuals of units without a centre are dropped. Returns the observed statistic.
moran500 <- function(keys, res) {
  k <- match(keys, ce$species)
  ok <- !is.na(k)
  D <- gc_km(ce$geo_latitude[k[ok]], ce$geo_longitude[k[ok]])
  ape::Moran.I(res[ok], (D > 0 & D <= 500) * 1)$observed
}

# --- Species table with the background and the species centres ---
d0 <- read_species_table()
for (cc in grep("^regional_background_", names(bg), value = TRUE))
  d0[[cc]] <- bg[[cc]][match(d0$pool_key, bg$species)]
d0 <- merge(d0, ce, by.x = "pool_key", by.y = "species", all.x = TRUE, sort = FALSE)

# --- Fit the models on each grafted tree ---
# `out` collects the contrast tables and `mor` the Moran's I values
out <- list()
mor <- list()
for (study in studies) {
  tr <- grafted[[study]]
  cw <- data.frame(analysis_species = tr$tip.label,
                   tree_tip_original = tr$tip.label,
                   matched = TRUE)
  on_tree <- d0[d0$species %in% tr$tip.label, ]

  for (m in names(measures)) for (pred in c("type", "breadth")) {
    # --- 1. Phylogenetic spatial GAM ---
    # log10 range ~ type (+ breadth) + s(lat, lon, bs = "sos", k = 100) + a species random
    # effect with phylogenetic covariance (tree correlation matrix C, penalised with C^-1
    # through paraPen) and an independent residual, i.e. a REML analogue of Pagel's lambda
    # plus a spatial smooth. k = 100 removes residual spatial autocorrelation (Moran's I
    # near 0); smaller k leave some. Type contrasts: single-step Tukey p-values (normal
    # approximation).

    # Units with a positive measure, a type and a centre
    g0 <- on_tree[is.finite(on_tree[[measures[[m]]]]) &
                    on_tree[[measures[[m]]]] > 0 &
                    !is.na(on_tree$interaction_type) &
                    is.finite(on_tree$geo_latitude), ]

    # The breadth model leaves out type n and units without a finite breadth
    if (pred == "breadth")
      g0 <- g0[g0$interaction_type != "n" & is.finite(g0$host_breadth), ]

    # One row per species, the tree pruned to them and their correlation matrix C
    g0 <- g0[!duplicated(g0$species), ]
    gtr <- ape::keep.tip(tr, g0$species)
    g0 <- g0[match(gtr$tip.label, g0$species), ]
    C <- ape::vcv(gtr, corr = TRUE)[g0$species, g0$species]

    # Response, type levels in use, centred breadth, and the species design matrix Z
    # (identity; penalised with the inverse of C in the fit)
    g0$y <- log10(g0[[measures[[m]]]])
    g0$interaction_type <- droplevels(g0$interaction_type)
    g0$hb <- g0$host_breadth - mean(g0$host_breadth)
    Z <- diag(nrow(g0))

    # Model formula and fit
    fo <- if (pred == "type")
      y ~ interaction_type + s(geo_latitude, geo_longitude, bs = "sos", k = 100) + Z else
      y ~ interaction_type + hb + s(geo_latitude, geo_longitude, bs = "sos", k = 100) + Z
    g <- gam(fo, data = c(as.list(g0), list(Z = Z)),
             paraPen = list(Z = list(solve(C))), method = "REML")

    # Coefficients, their covariance matrix and the type levels
    b <- coef(g)
    V <- vcov(g)
    lev <- levels(g0$interaction_type)

    # Contrast vector selecting the coefficient of type `a` (the first level is the
    # reference)
    cvec <- function(a) {
      v <- setNames(rep(0, length(b)), names(b))
      if (a != lev[1]) v[paste0("interaction_type", a)] <- 1
      v
    }

    if (pred == "type") {
      # All pairwise type contrasts as range ratios, with single-step Tukey intervals and
      # p-values (q975 is the critical value of the 95 % interval)
      gt <- rbindlist(lapply(combn(lev, 2, simplify = FALSE), function(q) {
        L <- cvec(q[1]) - cvec(q[2])
        e <- sum(L * b)
        se <- sqrt(drop(t(L) %*% V %*% L))
        q975 <- qtukey(0.95, nmeans = length(lev), df = Inf) / sqrt(2)
        data.table(contrast = paste(q, collapse = " - "),
                   ratio = 10^e,
                   lower = 10^(e - q975 * se),
                   upper = 10^(e + q975 * se),
                   p = ptukey(abs(e / se) * sqrt(2), nmeans = length(lev), df = Inf,
                              lower.tail = FALSE))
      }))

      # Moran's I of the residuals of the model
      mor[[paste("gam", study, m)]] <- data.table(
        model = "phylo_spatial_gam", study = study, measure = m, n = nrow(g0),
        moran_500 = moran500(g0$pool_key, residuals(g)))
    } else {
      # Breadth coefficient as a range ratio, with a normal-approximation interval and
      # p-value
      se <- sqrt(V["hb", "hb"])
      gt <- data.table(contrast = "breadth",
                       ratio = 10^b[["hb"]],
                       lower = 10^(b[["hb"]] - 1.96 * se),
                       upper = 10^(b[["hb"]] + 1.96 * se),
                       p = 2 * pnorm(-abs(b[["hb"]] / se)))
    }
    out[[paste("gam", study, m, pred)]] <- cbind(
      model = "phylo_spatial_gam", study = study, measure = m, predictors = pred,
      n = nrow(g0), n_parasite = sum(g0$interaction_type == "p"),
      n_grafted = sum(g0$species %in% attr(tr, "grafted")), gt)

    # --- 2. PGLS with the butterfly background ---
    # Adjusts for regional range-size structure, but its residuals stay spatially
    # autocorrelated, so its intervals are too narrow
    tax <- fit_log_range_models(on_tree, measures = measures[m],
                                regional_background = TRUE, breadth_scale = "raw")
    d <- tax$model_data[[paste(m, pred, sep = "_")]]
    meta <- tax$metadata[tax$metadata$predictors == pred, ]
    fo <- if (pred == "type")
      log10_range ~ interaction_type + regional_background_centered else
      log10_range ~ interaction_type + partner_breadth_centered +
        regional_background_centered
    fit <- fit_pagel_pgls(d, tr, cw, fo, study = study, measure = m, predictors = pred,
                          branch_treatment = "published", method = "REML",
                          breadth_reference_centered = if (pred == "breadth")
                            1 - meta$partner_breadth_mean else 0)

    # Type contrasts (type model) or the breadth coefficient (breadth model)
    ct <- as.data.table(fit$contrasts)[, .(contrast, ratio = range_ratio,
                                           lower = ratio_lower, upper = ratio_upper,
                                           p = p.value)]
    co <- as.data.table(fit$coefficients)[term == "partner_breadth_centered",
                                          .(contrast = "breadth", ratio = range_ratio,
                                            lower = ratio_lower, upper = ratio_upper,
                                            p = p_value)]
    out[[paste("bg", study, m, pred)]] <- cbind(
      model = "pgls_background", study = study, measure = m, predictors = pred,
      n = nrow(d), n_parasite = sum(d$interaction_type == "p"),
      n_grafted = sum(d$species %in% attr(tr, "grafted")),
      if (pred == "type") ct else co)

    # Moran's I of the normalised residuals (range-area type model only)
    if (pred == "type" && m == "area") {
      keys <- d$pool_key[match(fit$diagnostics$species, d$species)]
      mor[[paste("bg", study)]] <- data.table(
        model = "pgls_background_normalised_residuals", study = study, measure = m,
        n = nrow(d), moran_500 = moran500(keys, fit$diagnostics$normalized_residual))
    }
    cat(study, m, pred, "done", format(Sys.time(), "%H:%M:%S"), "\n")
  }

  # --- 3. Residual autocorrelation of the plain grafted PGLS (area, type model) ---
  tax0 <- fit_log_range_models(on_tree, measures = c(area = "range_area"),
                               breadth_scale = "raw")
  d <- tax0$model_data$area_type
  fit0 <- fit_pagel_pgls(d, tr, cw, log10_range ~ interaction_type, study = study,
                         measure = "area", predictors = "type",
                         branch_treatment = "published", method = "REML")
  keys <- d$pool_key[match(fit0$diagnostics$species, d$species)]
  mor[[paste("pgls", study)]] <- rbind(
    data.table(model = "pgls_raw_residuals", study = study, measure = "area", n = nrow(d),
               moran_500 = moran500(keys, fit0$diagnostics$residual)),
    data.table(model = "pgls_normalised_residuals", study = study, measure = "area",
               n = nrow(d),
               moran_500 = moran500(keys, fit0$diagnostics$normalized_residual)))
}

# --- Write the result tables ---
write_table(rbindlist(out, fill = TRUE),
            file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "phylo_geography_contrasts.csv"))
write_table(rbindlist(mor, fill = TRUE),
            file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "phylo_geography_moran.csv"))
print(rbindlist(mor, fill = TRUE))
```

```{r clear_fit_phylo_spatial_models, include=FALSE}
invisible(gc())
```

# Leave-one-genus-out

The range-area type model (mixed model and grafted PGLS on both trees) is refitted after omitting each genus with at least three parasites in the main model.

*Inputs:* s03/species_table.csv; grafted_trees.rds, lmm_contrasts.csv, pgls_grafted_contrasts.csv  
*Output:* leave_genus_out.csv (one row per omitted genus x model x contrast; dropped = "none" is the full model and must reproduce the main mixed model and the grafted PGLS)

```{r fit_leave_genus_out}
# --- Grafted trees and species table ---
grafted <- readRDS(file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "grafted_trees.rds"))
d_all <- read_species_table()

# Contrasts kept in the output
keep_contrasts <- c("f-p", "n-p", "m-p", "f-m")

# --- Genera to omit ---
# Parasitic genera of the main range-area type model
fit0 <- fit_log_range_models(d_all, measures = c(area = "range_area"),
                             breadth_scale = "raw")
md0 <- fit0$model_data$area_type
pgen <- sort(table(md0$genus[md0$interaction_type == "p"]), decreasing = TRUE)

# Omission sets: none (the full model) and each genus with at least three parasites
drops <- c(list(none = character()),
           setNames(as.list(names(pgen)[pgen >= 3]), names(pgen)[pgen >= 3]))
print(pgen)

# --- Contrast table of a model ---
# Kept contrasts of a model as a table with ratio, interval and p-value; spaces are
# removed from the contrast labels
tidy <- function(ct) {
  x <- as.data.table(ct)[, contrast := gsub(" ", "", contrast)][
    contrast %in% keep_contrasts]
  x[, .(contrast, ratio = range_ratio, lower = ratio_lower, upper = ratio_upper,
        p = p.value)]
}

# --- Refit the models omitting each genus ---
res <- list()
for (k in names(drops)) {
  d <- d_all[!d_all$genus %in% drops[[k]], ]

  # Taxonomic mixed model
  tax <- fit_log_range_models(d, measures = c(area = "range_area"), breadth_scale = "raw")
  md <- tax$model_data$area_type
  res[[paste(k, "lmm")]] <- cbind(
    dropped = k, model = "lmm", n = nrow(md),
    n_parasite = sum(md$interaction_type == "p"), lambda = NA_real_,
    tidy(tax$contrasts[tax$contrasts$predictors == "type", ]))

  # Grafted PGLS on each tree
  for (study in studies) {
    tr <- grafted[[study]]
    cw <- data.frame(analysis_species = tr$tip.label,
                     tree_tip_original = tr$tip.label,
                     matched = TRUE)
    taxp <- fit_log_range_models(d[d$species %in% tr$tip.label, ],
                                 measures = c(area = "range_area"), breadth_scale = "raw")
    dm <- taxp$model_data$area_type
    fit <- fit_pagel_pgls(dm, tr, cw, log10_range ~ interaction_type, study = study,
                          measure = "area", predictors = "type",
                          branch_treatment = "published", method = "REML")
    res[[paste(k, study)]] <- cbind(dropped = k, model = paste0("pgls_", study),
                                    n = nrow(dm),
                                    n_parasite = sum(dm$interaction_type == "p"),
                                    lambda = fit$metadata$lambda, tidy(fit$contrasts))
    cat(k, study, "n =", nrow(dm), "lambda =", round(fit$metadata$lambda, 2),
        format(Sys.time(), "%H:%M:%S"), "\n")
  }
}

# --- Collect the results ---
out <- rbindlist(res, fill = TRUE)
out[, dropped_genera := vapply(dropped,
                               function(k) paste(drops[[k]], collapse = ";"),
                               "")]

# --- Check the full fits ---
# The full fits (dropped = "none") must reproduce the main mixed models and the grafted
# PGLS above
ref_lmm <- fread(file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "lmm_contrasts.csv"))[
  table == main_table & analysis == "main" & measure == "area" & predictors == "type"]
ref_pg <- fread(file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "pgls_grafted_contrasts.csv"))[
  measure == "area" & predictors == "type"]
chk <- rbind(
  merge(out[dropped == "none" & model == "lmm", .(contrast, ratio)],
        ref_lmm[, .(contrast = gsub(" ", "", contrast), ref = range_ratio)],
        by = "contrast"),
  rbindlist(lapply(studies, function(s)
    merge(out[dropped == "none" & model == paste0("pgls_", s), .(contrast, ratio)],
          ref_pg[study == s, .(contrast = gsub(" ", "", contrast), ref = range_ratio)],
          by = "contrast"))))
# Four contrasts for the mixed model and for each tree
stopifnot(nrow(chk) == 4L * (1L + length(studies)),
          max(abs(chk$ratio / chk$ref - 1)) < 1e-6)

# --- Write and print the results ---
write_table(out, file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "leave_genus_out.csv"))
print(out[, .(dropped, model, n_parasite, contrast, ratio = round(ratio, 2),
              p = signif(p, 2))])
```

# Genus-level PGLS

Genus by interaction-type units, represented by one species each on the grafted trees, test whether small ranges recur across parasitic lineages; with all genera and without *Lepidochrysops*.

*Inputs:* s03/species_table.csv; grafted_trees.rds  
*Output:* genus_level_pgls.csv (n-f stored as f-n, as in the other result tables)

```{r fit_genus_level_pgls}
# --- Species table, grafted trees and omission sets ---
d_all <- read_species_table()
grafted <- readRDS(file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "grafted_trees.rds"))

# All genera, and without Lepidochrysops
drops <- list(none = character(), Lepidochrysops = "Lepidochrysops")

# All six contrasts of the Tukey family
keep <- c("f-p", "n-p", "m-p", "f-m", "n-f", "n-m")

# --- Main mixed models and contrast table ---
# Main mixed models of the three measures; their type-model data give the genus-level units
fit0 <- fit_log_range_models(d_all, measures = measures, breadth_scale = "raw")

# Kept contrasts of a model as a table with ratio, interval and p-value. Spaces are
# removed from the contrast labels, and n-f is stored as f-n (ratio inverted), as in the
# other result tables.
tidy <- function(x) {
  x <- as.data.table(x)[, contrast := gsub(" ", "", contrast)][contrast %in% keep]
  x <- x[, .(contrast, ratio = range_ratio, lower = ratio_lower, upper = ratio_upper,
             p = p.value)]
  x[contrast == "n-f",
    `:=`(contrast = "f-n", ratio = 1 / ratio, lower = 1 / upper, upper = 1 / lower)]
  x
}

# --- Fit a PGLS to the genus-level units of each measure, omission set and tree ---
res <- list()
for (m in names(measures)) {
  # Units of genus x subfamily x type: mean log10 range and member species
  md <- as.data.table(fit0$model_data[[paste0(m, "_type")]])
  u0 <- md[, .(y = mean(log10_range),
               species_list = paste(sort(species), collapse = ";")),
           by = .(genus, subfamily, interaction_type)]

  for (k in names(drops)) {
    u <- u0[!genus %in% drops[[k]]]
    u[, interaction_type := factor(interaction_type, levels = c("n", "f", "m", "p"))]

    for (study in studies) {
      # One species represents each unit: a matched tip if the unit has one, otherwise its
      # grafted tip (which sits at the genus node), so no relationship within genera is
      # assumed; units of genera absent from the tree are omitted
      tr <- grafted[[study]]
      gr <- attr(tr, "grafted")
      rep <- vapply(u$species_list, function(s) {
        sp <- intersect(strsplit(s, ";", fixed = TRUE)[[1]], tr$tip.label)
        if (!length(sp)) return(NA_character_)
        mt <- setdiff(sp, gr)
        if (length(mt)) sort(mt)[1] else sort(sp)[1]
      }, "")
      ud <- data.frame(species = unname(rep), log10_range = u$y,
                       interaction_type = u$interaction_type, genus = u$genus)
      ud <- ud[!is.na(ud$species), ]

      # Tree pruned to the representatives, and the PGLS of the units
      gt <- ape::keep.tip(tr, ud$species)
      cw <- data.frame(analysis_species = gt$tip.label,
                       tree_tip_original = gt$tip.label,
                       matched = TRUE)
      f2 <- fit_pagel_pgls(ud, gt, cw, log10_range ~ interaction_type, study = study,
                           measure = m, predictors = "type",
                           branch_treatment = "published", method = "REML")
      res[[paste(m, k, study)]] <- cbind(
        analysis = "genus_pgls", tree = study, measure = m, dropped = k,
        n_units = nrow(ud), n_p_units = sum(ud$interaction_type == "p"),
        lambda = f2$metadata$lambda, tidy(f2$contrasts))
    }
    cat(m, k, "done", format(Sys.time(), "%H:%M:%S"), "\n")
  }
}

# --- Write the result table ---
write_table(rbindlist(res, fill = TRUE),
            file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "genus_level_pgls.csv"))
```

```{r clear_fit_genus_level_pgls, include=FALSE}
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), setup_objects))
invisible(gc())
```
